newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Woman to take on warlords for Liberia presidency.
newsitem.headline: Woman to take on warlords for Liberia presidency.

text.p: U.N. Development Programme Africa director Ellen-Johnson Sirleaf returned home to Liberia on Friday and announced she planned to run for president against the West African nation's warlords on May 30.
"I have come to say 'yes' to your call that I lead our country and save it from falling in the hands of the wrong people," she told several thousand supporters at Monrovia's Spriggs Payne airfield.
Sirleaf has joined the Unity Party, which was expected to choose her as its candidate at a convention on Saturday.
Charles Taylor, who launched the war in 1989, and faction rivals Alhaji Kromah and George Boley have already thrown their hats in the ring.

Presidential and parliamentary elections on May 30 are part of a peace plan brokered by Liberia's West African neighbours. West African peacekeepers have gone a long way towards disarming the rival faction fighters.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The war has killed well over 150,000 people and shattered Liberia's rubber and mineral-based economy.
